In 0.2.3 and earlier it jumps to a bad address in its first second and stops. The cause is in the game: it asks for a cartridge copy of 0 bytes, which the console reads as 16 MB, and that copy overwrites its own memory (its notes say it glitches on a real N64 too, and runs on Project64). Fixed for the next version: Joey64 skips that copy for this game, as Project64 does, and it plays at full speed (Odin 2 Portal, Odin 3).

column3: Runs (Retroid Pocket Flip, 2026-11-12). The earlier close on the Odin 3 Portal was a fault in the test setup, not the game.

Hung before its first frame until 2026-11-12: this Wii Virtual Console copy kept the cartridge's header checksum over changed code, so the boot code never finished. Since core rel2 c994aa7 Joey64 boots it with the right checksum (checked on the Retroid Pocket Flip and Duo).

No picture after its first frame up to 0.2.2. Fixed in 0.2.3: the RSP now starts each of its tasks the way the console does; it plays at full speed (Odin 2 Portal).

A bug in the game: it writes a display list past the end of the memory it set aside for it, and the next things it sets aside overwrite it. On a real N64 the CPU's cache hides this; Joey64, like other mupen64plus emulators, has no CPU cache, so the picture stays black. Emulators that copy the cache (ares, CEN64) run it.
